one_line: Agent-assisted, human-guarded overdue invoice recovery workspace.
what_it_does: Prioritizes overdue payments and supports guarded plans, reminders, payment handoffs, status updates, and audit trails.
leverage_rationale: Structured page-local state and guarded sequencing appear materially better than an agent scraping a dashboard, though the packet lacks a live demonstration.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes prioritized invoices, guarded recovery plans, payment handoffs, and auditable recovery.
About text explicitly frames WebMCP as enabling page-local state and safe sequencing.
execution_rationale: The described scope is coherent, but there are no submitted video frames or transcript and only packaging evidence, so end-to-end completion is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and repository is public.
No video submitted; Devpost screenshot is packaging evidence only.
impact_rationale: Small businesses and independent professionals have a concrete cash-flow and follow-up problem that this workflow directly targets.
impact_evidence: Pitch names small businesses and overdue-invoice prioritization.
Description identifies freelancers, tutors, consultants, and agencies as users.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful human-supervised recovery workflow is a useful synthesis, though the underlying invoice-recovery category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Guarded reminders, payment handoffs, promise-to-pay states, and audit trail form a coherent agent workflow.
usability_note: Promising controlled workflow; actual usability cannot be checked from the packet.
red_flags: No video or functional visual evidence submitted.
standouts: Human control over sensitive customer communication.
Auditability is central rather than incidental.
advance_reason: Strong audience/problem fit and plausible WebMCP value, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Governed observe-act-verify receipts for autonomous agents in 3D scenes.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect, authorize, execute, re-observe, verify, and receipt spatial changes under bounded permissions.
leverage_rationale: Spatial state is difficult to drive reliably through generic UI automation; the explicit observe-act-see-again-verify loop and governed receipts make structured agent access central.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states agents can understand, change, re-observe, and verify 3D environments.
About text specifies bounded capabilities, denied restricted actions, and execution receipts.
Frame sheets visibly show a 3D virtual-production-studio interface and tool/receipt-oriented screens.
execution_rationale: The concept, visual 3D studio, permission boundary, and verification loop are coherent and appear substantially implemented, with some end-to-end evidence limitation because no transcript was supplied.
execution_evidence: Three submitted video frame sheets show the spatial application across states.
About text describes protected-scene behavior and a concrete studio objective.
impact_rationale: Auditable spatial agency is valuable for virtual production, simulation, robotics, and other 3D workflows, though the packet does not establish a specific deployed audience beyond the demo.
impact_evidence: Concrete virtual production studio scenario.
Receipts and authorization address real safety/accountability needs for spatial automation.
creativity_rationale: The governed observe-act-verify interaction model for 3D environments is novel, memorable, and pursued coherently.
creativity_evidence: Explicit Observe → Act → See Again → Verify → Receipt loop.
Permission-governed spatial actions and post-action verification are distinctive.
usability_note: Clear safety model, though spatial-agent setup may be specialized.
red_flags: No transcript; exact agent interaction is only partially visible.
standouts: Strongest structured-state and accountability rationale in the packet.
Denied actions preserve protected scene state.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated agent-native spatial workflow with strong visual coherence.

one_line: A probe harness measuring schema enforcement failures in WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Enumerates reference-demo tools, generates forbidden inputs, executes probes, and records mismatches between schemas and runtime acceptance.
leverage_rationale: The structured tool surface enables systematic, repeatable schema probing that would be substantially more error-prone through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Claims 225 of 289 probes across 23 tools and 17 of 17 imperative tools accepted forbidden input.
About text describes getTools enumeration, schema-derived adversarial inputs, and recorded outcomes.
Frame sheets visibly show probe/report-style developer interfaces.
execution_rationale: The measurement target, probe taxonomy, and reported aggregate findings are unusually concrete and coherent; visual evidence supports a working analysis harness.
execution_evidence: Vendored official reference demos are specified as targets.
Concrete probe counts and categories are reported.
Three video frame sheets show the tool-analysis/reporting workflow.
impact_rationale: Schema non-enforcement is a credible reliability and security concern for tool authors and agent ecosystems, and this project provides actionable evidence.
impact_evidence: Targets official demos used to teach WebMCP.
Tests type mismatches, enum/range violations, omissions, long strings, control characters, and prompt-like text.
creativity_rationale: Turning a discovered contract gap into a systematic empirical probe suite is a fresh and technically ambitious hackathon direction.
creativity_evidence: Measures promises versus actual acceptance rather than merely building another consumer app.
Adversarial input generation is broad and purposeful.
usability_note: Potentially valuable to tool authors; the packet does not show how findings are consumed or remediated.
red_flags: Reported counts differ between pitch and about text (225/289 versus 299/23 tools), creating a minor evidence-consistency issue.
standouts: Concrete empirical result against official reference implementations.
Excellent alignment between WebMCP and the testing method.
advance_reason: High-value, technically specific investigation with credible evidence and strong WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Wardrobe try-on and outfit planning with agent-assisted styling.
what_it_does: Uses a personal wardrobe/photo context for try-ons, outfit suggestions, weather and schedule planning, shopping gaps, calendars, and exports.
leverage_rationale: Agent-level planning actions are useful, but the product was pre-existing and the same visible operations appear broadly achievable through UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text says only WebMCP support was built during the hackathon.
Tools represent goals such as plan an outfit rather than individual buttons.
execution_rationale: The live pre-existing product and three frame sheets suggest a coherent, usable experience, but hackathon-added agent flows are not clearly demonstrated end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive with three submitted frame sheets.
About text explicitly distinguishes existing product from new WebMCP support.
impact_rationale: Online shoppers and wardrobe planners have a real convenience and decision-support use case, with personal styling value.
impact_evidence: Try-on and wardrobe-based outfit planning address a clear consumer desire.
Calendar, weather, and missing-item planning connect to practical routines.
creativity_rationale: The combination of virtual closet, try-on, and agent planning is a competent new angle on a familiar fashion tool category.
creativity_evidence: Agent suggests outfits from wardrobe plus weather and schedule and keeps plans user-editable.
usability_note: Existing web/mobile/extension product and visible polished UI suggest good usability; added agent reliability is unverified.
red_flags: Core product predates the hackathon; only the WebMCP layer is new.
No transcript and agent invocation is not established.
standouts: Goal-oriented tools rather than button mirroring.
User remains able to see, edit, and control the plan.
advance_reason: Useful product, but WebMCP delta and novelty are modest compared with stronger entries.

one_line: Client-side PDF redaction and form filling through agent-callable tools.
what_it_does: Finds and previews redactions for confirmation, flattens them into a PDF, and fills only stated form values without inventing omissions.
leverage_rationale: Precise document operations are significantly safer and more reliable as structured tools than an agent guessing at a PDF viewer UI, especially with confirmation gates.
leverage_evidence: Pitch contrasts real PDF tools with guessing at the UI.
About text describes match finding, review cards, flattening, field-by-field filling, and client-side processing.
Three frame sheets visibly show PDF/document workflows and redaction/form states.
execution_rationale: Two focused workflows, review-before-apply behavior, and concrete privacy semantics form a coherent product; frames support the main UI but do not fully prove agent calls.
execution_evidence: Five gallery images and three video frame sheets are supplied.
Redact and fill workflows have explicit confirmation and download endpoints.
About text states 100% client-side document handling.
impact_rationale: People handling loan, financial, and other sensitive PDFs have a concrete accuracy and privacy need that the product addresses directly.
impact_evidence: Examples include redacting loan/account details and filling a loan application.
Document remains in the tab; omitted form values are left blank.
creativity_rationale: Agent-operated PDF editing with safety-preserving review is a fresh, well-scoped application of WebMCP, though PDF editing itself is established.
creativity_evidence: Moves beyond PDF reading to actionable redaction and form workflows.
Human confirmation before irreversible flattening is integrated into the interaction.
usability_note: Natural-language workflows and review cards appear approachable; API-key/extension setup may add friction.
red_flags: The packet does not fully expose the exact model/extension access path.
standouts: Strong privacy boundary and non-hallucinating form behavior.
Clear human approval point for destructive edits.
advance_reason: High practical value and strong structured-action delta, supported by coherent visual evidence.

one_line: Neuroinclusive water-cycle learning interface adapted by a browser agent.
what_it_does: Adapts density, text size, colors, motion, animation, audio, and response channels while requiring human confirmation before academic submission.
leverage_rationale: Live, coordinated adaptation of a learning interface to a student's needs is a meaningful structured-agent role, especially with a safety boundary around submission.
leverage_evidence: About text lists five imperative tools and real-time adaptation dimensions.
Voice, text, and visual response channels are supported.
Frame sheets visibly show the character-led educational interface in multiple visual states.
execution_rationale: The prototype has a clear narrative, visual identity, adaptation scope, and explicit safety boundary, but the packet does not demonstrate a full lesson completion.
execution_evidence: Three submitted frame sheets show the learning experience.
Concrete Leo/Luma/Ayu scenario and deployed client-side implementation are described.
impact_rationale: Neurodivergent students face a specific, consequential accessibility problem, and adapting presentation while preserving the learning goal directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Description identifies overload, dense instructions, time pressure, motion, and single response modes as barriers.
Agent can tailor multiple interface dimensions without changing the academic objective.
Submission cannot be automated without student/adult confirmation.
creativity_rationale: The learning-goal/path separation and character-led adaptive interaction are an original, ambitious application of agentic UI adaptation.
creativity_evidence: Neuroinclusive adaptation is treated as an interaction model, not merely a visual theme.
Safety-aware preparation/review flow is built into the concept.
usability_note: Calm multimodal presentation is promising for the intended users; actual student testing is not shown.
red_flags: No transcript and no evidence of real student evaluation.
standouts: Strong accessibility-centered product thesis.
Human confirmation prevents an agent from submitting academic work.
advance_reason: Exceptional audience/problem fit and thoughtful adaptive interaction with credible prototype evidence.

one_line: Private browser-native structured research workspace shared with agents.
what_it_does: Builds outlines linking notes and sources, validates/querys structured research, and lets agents suggest improvements for human review.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured browser state and reviewable suggestions improve agent collaboration over scraping a document, but the core research editing outcome remains possible with other interfaces.
leverage_evidence: No login, plugin, or server setup is required according to the pitch.
About text describes agents reading research and suggesting improvements with user-controlled application.
Frame sheets visibly show structured research/editor views.
execution_rationale: The product has a clear information model, example research pages, and a described Swift/WASM validation kernel, with moderate visual evidence but no transcript.
execution_evidence: Three submitted frame sheets show research-page/editor states.
About text specifies type hierarchy, links/notes, and separate WASM reader.
impact_rationale: Researchers, students, and knowledge workers can benefit from private structured outlines and agent-assisted review, though the packet gives limited proof of depth in the workflows.
impact_evidence: Use case centers on organizing links, notes, people, posts, videos, and sources.
Human reviews agent suggestions before applying changes.
creativity_rationale: A portable, browser-private research graph with agent collaboration is a fresh synthesis beyond ordinary notes, though adjacent tools exist.
creativity_evidence: No-login WebMCP sharing and explicit type/connection hierarchy.
Portable Swift kernel plus WASM reader is ambitious for the scope.
usability_note: No-setup/private positioning is strong; information modeling may impose learning cost.
red_flags: Claims are stronger than the limited end-to-end evidence supplied.
standouts: Private browser-local data with agent-readable shared state.
Review-before-apply collaboration model.
advance_reason: Solid research collaboration concept with meaningful shared-state value and credible implementation detail.

one_line: Parametric 3D pottery editor whose deterministic geometry engine exports buildable templates.
what_it_does: Lets humans or agents adjust vessel parameters and deterministically generate precise multipage printable clay templates with reversible changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP pairs an agent's flexible design reasoning with a deterministic geometry/export engine and shared reversible state, avoiding unreliable agent-generated templates.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says the app, not the agent, guarantees precise deterministic geometry and export.
Transcript shows agent-driven parameter change arriving in the editor and undo/redo shared across human and agent.
Three frame sheets visibly show the 3D editor and template/document output.
execution_rationale: The 179-second video has a coherent explanation and demonstrates the central workflow from agent prompt to changed design, with reversible state and export-oriented UI.
execution_evidence: Video transcript describes live pairing, parameter change, and visible update.
Frame sheets show 3D vessel editing and printable/document views.
About text explains deterministic multipage PDF output.
impact_rationale: Potters and makers have a concrete pain point: inaccurate templates cause wasted material and studio time; deterministic output directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text describes cereal-box template practice and failures discovered after hours of building.
Examples include volume and vessel-style changes while preserving buildability.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent division of labor—AI for complex design intent, deterministic software for fabrication geometry—is memorable and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Cross-browser pairing via websocket and shared undo/redo extend the interaction model.
usability_note: Human-editable parameters and reversible agent changes make a complex fabrication workflow approachable; pairing adds setup complexity.
red_flags: Transcript is occasionally uncertain/garbled, but the central demonstration is clear.
standouts: Exceptional deterministic-engine/agent collaboration boundary.
Reversible shared state across human and paired agent browser.
advance_reason: One of the clearest examples of WebMCP changing what an agent can reliably accomplish.

one_line: Moodle plugin exposing grounded course and study tools to ChatGPT in-browser.
what_it_does: Retrieves assignments/materials, creates adaptive study schedules, and critiques essays against official rubrics without extra student setup.
leverage_rationale: Page-local access to authenticated course context without separate API keys or integration setup is a meaningful agent advantage, though the tools are conventional information operations.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says tools run inside the active browser session with no setup.
About text specifies Moodle navigation integration and four student-focused workflows.
Three frame sheets show Moodle/course and ChatGPT-oriented states.
execution_rationale: A real Moodle plugin and deployed stack are described with a coherent tool set, but no transcript and no gallery images limit direct proof of the central workflow.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo are reported.
Implementation details name PHP plugin hooks, AMD loader, Moodle 5.2.2, and deployment.
Video frame sheets supplied, though not a transcript.
impact_rationale: Students and instructors have a clear need for grounded course help, assignment retrieval, study planning, and rubric-based feedback.
impact_evidence: Problem is grounded in scattered Moodle course content.
Tools use course materials and official grading rubrics rather than generic answers.
creativity_rationale: The Moodle-to-WebMCP integration is useful and well targeted, but the interaction model is a familiar educational assistant pattern.
creativity_evidence: No-setup browser integration and rubric-grounded critique are practical differentiators.
usability_note: Familiar ChatGPT interface and no additional student setup are strong usability choices.
red_flags: No gallery images or transcript; end-to-end agent behavior is not fully inspectable.
standouts: Grounded access to institutional course context without API-key friction.
Useful student/instructor split.

one_line: Floor-plan studio where agents run accessibility measurements and propose geometry fixes.
what_it_does: Analyzes routes, door clearances, turning circles, and reachability, then proposes and previews approved plan modifications.
leverage_rationale: A geometry engine exposed as structured tools lets an agent perform reliable spatial measurement and iterative checks that image/UI-driving agents handle poorly.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states humans draw while agents measure.
Transcript demonstrates wheelchair and walking-frame checks, numeric failures, and an agent-generated fix requiring approval.
Frame sheets visibly show floor-plan editor, measurements, and modification states.
execution_rationale: The 173-second video directly demonstrates the central workflow from untouched plan to accessibility diagnosis to proposed and approved fixes.
execution_evidence: Transcript includes concrete 760/815 mm and 800/900 mm measurements and turning-circle results.
Video shows agent operation without human clicks until approval.
Three frame sheets support editor/result states.
impact_rationale: Home accessibility assessment is a high-consequence real need for wheelchair users, carers, injured homeowners, and small landlords; numeric diagnosis and fixes directly address it.
impact_evidence: About text names adapting homes, assessing flats, and accessibility retrofits.
Demonstration identifies an unreachable bathroom and missing kitchen turning circle.
User can upload plans and approve changes.
creativity_rationale: The human-draw/agent-measure interaction is a memorable and original use of WebMCP, with a concrete safety-aware edit loop.
creativity_evidence: Agent is used for iterative spatial reasoning against a real geometry engine, not image interpretation.
Proposed changes are previewed and explicitly approved.
usability_note: The division between familiar drawing and agent measurement is clear; interpreting standards and proposed edits still needs user care.
red_flags: Accessibility thresholds are presented as demo figures; standards jurisdiction should be clarified in production.
standouts: Exceptional end-to-end evidence.
High-consequence use case with measurable, inspectable outputs and approval gates.
advance_reason: Top-tier combination of indispensable WebMCP leverage, demonstrated execution, and real accessibility impact.
